content: The WikiDoc platform includes a reference manager that enables users to insert references using their PubMed ID numbers. When text is moved within the document, the associated reference moves along with it. All references are automatically compiled and displayed at the bottom of the article. By clicking on a reference, users are directed to the corresponding article, making the process straightforward and efficient. In traditional referencing methods, users typically insert a number in the text (e.g., (1) or 1) to indicate a citation and then manually type the reference details at the end of the article. However, this is not the preferred method in WikiDoc. Instead, WikiDoc employs an automated reference manager with several advantages: References are automatically numbered. References move dynamically with the text. Clicking on a reference takes the user directly to the cited article. Unlike the manual method of adding references at the end of the article, the WikiDoc reference manager allows users to insert a code for the reference immediately after the relevant text. This is achieved using a software program that generates the necessary reference code. The process of using the WikiDoc reference manager involves the following steps: 1. Use PubMed to locate the desired article. 2. Copy the PubMed ID (PMID) number, which is typically found at the bottom of the article's abstract. The PMID can be located using the search function in browsers like Firefox or Internet Explorer. It appears in the format PMID: 19032997. 3. Paste the PMID into a software program that generates Wiki language code for the reference. Several tools are available for this purpose, including: SUMSearch Biomedical Citation Maker (converts PMID into Wiki reference markup with embedded SUMSearch links). DOI Wikipedia reference generator (converts DOI into Wiki reference markup). DTU Informatics PMID to Cite journal (converts PMID into Wiki reference markup). OttoBib (converts ISBN into Wiki reference markup). Dave's Template Filler (converts DrugBank ID, HGNC ID, ISBN, PubMed ID, PubMed Central ID, PubChem ID, or URLs into Wiki reference markup). 4. Ensure the add ref tag button is checked in the reference manager software. 5. Submit the information to generate the Wiki language code. 6. Copy the generated Wiki language code from the software program. For example, the output for PMID 19032997 might look like this: ``` {{cite journal | author = Gibson CM, Pride YB, Frederick PD, ''et al.'' | title = Trends in reperfusion strategies, door-to-needle and door-to-balloon times, and in-hospital mortality among patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction enrolled in the National Registry of Myocardial Infarction from 1990 to 2006 | journal = Am. Heart J. | url = }} ``` 7. Paste the generated code into the text where the superscript number for the reference should appear. For instance, the text might read: Gibson et al. recently summarized the improvements made in clinical outcomes as a result of 15 years of quality improvement efforts in the NRMI registry {{cite journal | author = Gibson CM, Pride YB, Frederick PD, ''et al.'' | title = Trends in reperfusion strategies, door-to-needle and door-to-balloon times, and in-hospital mortality among patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction enrolled in the National Registry of Myocardial Infarction from 1990 to 2006 | journal = Am. Heart J. | url = }}. This would generate a reference in the text that appears as: Gibson et al. recently summarized the improvements made in clinical outcomes as a result of 15 years of quality improvement efforts in the NRMI registry. ↑ Gibson CM, Pride YB, Frederick PD; et al. (2008). 'Trends in reperfusion strategies, door-to-needle and door-to-balloon times, and in-hospital mortality among patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction enrolled in the National Registry of Myocardial Infarction from 1990 to 2006.' Am. Heart J. 156(6): 1035–44. PMID 19032997. If users prefer not to use the reference manager, they can manually type references. To do so: 1. Insert a footnote number immediately after the sentence where the reference is needed. 2. Type the reference text between `<ref>` tags. For example: ``` <ref>Author Name. Title of the Article. Journal Name. Year; Volume(Issue): Page Numbers.</ref> ``` This will appear as a footnote in the text. If the same manual reference is used multiple times, it is necessary to assign a name to the reference to avoid duplication. Without a name, each instance of the reference will be treated as unique, resulting in multiple entries for the same source. To make references appear at the bottom of the article, the following code should be included: ``` <references /> ``` This will generate a reference list in small font, formatted in two columns, with links to the original articles and abstracts. The output will look like this: ↑ J Fam Pract. 2000 Oct;49(10):921-3.
